chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Jimmy Noone: his death, golf, family and California
summary: Zutty praised Jimmy Noone, who died on the way to an Orson Welles broadcast rehearsal, loved California and golf, and had children by a second marriage.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now Jimmy Noon, how did you get on
with Jimmy? Were you old buddies, or?

Oh fine. Lovely. Because you know when we were playing that Orson Welles show, that Mobil Oil? And we got word that Jimmy had died you know. Dropped dead getting ready to come to rehearsal. And Orson Welles preached his funeral right over there. And that was really something.
But Jimmy never really got the sort of credit he deserved did he?
No, no.
I don't think so. He was a great man.
But didn't he sort of spend most of his life in Chicago? I mean he didn't travel much did he?

Yes. He didn't travel much. But he got to California and he fell in love with California. He was so crazy about California. He was so happy. And he was a great golfer you know. Yes, he played fine golf. He used to play all the pros, all the black pros you know in Chicago and everything. And he had a girlfriend that was a great golfer also. See and......
Well I mean, did he have, did he have a family in Chicago?
Why sure.
Well I mean that's why he stayed was it?
Yes. But his wife then was a Creole girl from New Orleans but then he married again.
Oh I see.
See after his wife, him and his wife separated or she passed away or something. Then he married again and then he had.....
Married a young girl.
A younger girl, one of the Matthews. She was related to my first wife's people. She was a relation you know. And he had two boys and a girl.
Yes, one of the boys still lives here in New York. And the girl is teaching school in Cincinnati. She's married.
And one tried to be a clarinet player like his father you know. But he was really played more tenor, tenor saxophone than he did clarinet.
But when he came to California they were babies really. Just, well one of them was a baby in arms when he came. The other two were just toddlers. Now they are grown up and have families of
their own. We saw one boy in California when Zutt went out there to play for the Berkeley colleges you know.
